title: Don Dale detainee isolated for 84 hours and denied food as coercion technique, investigation finds
summary: Children’s commissioner says young Indigenous person kept in isolation for 12 hours longer than permitted under NT youth justice laws because they refused to move cell blocks Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast A young Aboriginal person detained at the Don Dale detention centre was kept in isolation for 84 hours, unable to leave their cell or make contact with any support person, and was denied food for some of that time as a coercion tactic by officers, an investigation by the Northern Territory’s Office of the Children’s Commissioner has found. The investigation examined an incident that took place in April 2024 at the notorious youth detention facility in Berrimah in the NT, which saw a young detainee held in a cell after refusing to move from one cell block to another.
